counterfactual_missing_items: No sicca symptoms or Sjögren-specific organ involvement to support R2
No RA-ILD-specific pulmonary pattern or lung biopsy to support R4
No autoimmune-hepatitis-specific antibodies or liver histology to support R6
decisive_items: heliotrope rash and erythematous lip swelling
Positive myositis panel for anti-SAE antibodies
response.rationale: R1 is strongly supported by the raw skin signs, proximal weakness, elevated CK, anti-SAE antibodies, and Wong-type skin biopsy. R4 uses only rheumatoid arthritis history and nonspecific CT opacities, which cannot explain the heliotrope rash and myopathy. R2 relies on a weak, nonspecific anti-SSA finding, and R6 only on hepatitis history with transaminitis.

rejected.why: Only anti-SSA positivity is non-specific and no raw support spans are supplied; it does not explain the myositis, heliotrope rash, or CK elevation.
Hepatitis B/C history and elevated transaminases are nonspecific findings and do not establish autoimmune hepatitis without specific serology or histology.
